new_scholarship.name: Türkiye Scholarships (Türkiye Bursları) — Government Scholarship Programme of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities
new_scholarship.official_source: Türkiye Scholarships — Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB), Republic of Türkiye
new_scholarship.duration: Full-time degree programmes (associate, bachelor's, master's, doctoral)
new_scholarship.deadline: Applications 10 January – 20 February each year (2026 cycle: 10 January – 20 February 2026)
new_scholarship.application_period: One annual period, 10 January – 20 February, for all degree levels; Research Scholarships and Success Scholarships run on separate periods
new_scholarship.description: Türkiye Scholarships is a government-funded, competitive scholarship programme run under the coordination of the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities (YTB) that places international scholarship holders in Turkish universities. The official 2026 announcement states it is open to citizens of all countries and to applicants seeking associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees, with applications received in a single annual period from 10 January to 20 February. The programme funds tuition fees, a monthly stipend, health insurance, accommodation, a one-off flight ticket and a Turkish language course, and includes university and department placement. Short-term Research Scholarships and Success Scholarships are separate sub-programmes with their own application periods announced on the same official site.
benefits: Monthly stipend paid throughout the study period
Full tuition fee coverage at the host public university
Health insurance provided by the programme
Accommodation in university dormitories
One-off international flight ticket
Free Turkish language course (1 year)
Free academic, social and cultural programmes
University and department placement arranged by YTB
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Citizens of all countries are eligible. Turkish citizens and former Turkish citizens are excluded, as are applicants already enrolled at a Turkish university at the level for which they apply. Merit Scholarship candidates additionally need very high school leaving examination, language and academic qualification scores; Research Scholarships require researchers and academics.
eligibility: Citizens of all countries
Graduates, or those due to graduate before August of the application year
Researchers and academics (for Research Scholarships)
Not a Turkish citizen or a person who has lost Turkish citizenship
Not already enrolled in a programme at a Turkish university at the level applied for
application_method: Online application through the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS), free of charge
Register, upload the required documents and submit through the TBBS portal
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Competitive and merit-based, with a strong emphasis on candidates' academic excellence. Assessment involves a documentary evaluation process followed by an interview period; results are announced in early August for the general round.
new_scholarship.english_requirement: Not required for the general scholarship. Proof of language proficiency (for example TOEFL IBT 80/120 or IELTS 6.5/9.0) is required only for the Merit Scholarship Programme, which also requires a minimum weighted average of 90% and a top-10 national examination rank.
new_scholarship.notes: Programme is fully funded but admission is separate from funding: candidates apply for the scholarship through TBBS and YTB assigns the university and department. Turkish language study is compulsory in year one.
new_scholarship.funding_period: per month (stipend) plus one-off flight ticket

programme_detail_official.description: Türkiye Scholarships is a government-funded, competitive scholarship programme awarded by the Presidency of Turks Abroad and Related Communities to outstanding students and researchers to pursue full-time or short-term programmes at the top universities in Türkiye. The programme is open to applicants from all countries and covers associate, bachelor's, master's and doctoral degrees, providing financial support, tuition fee, accommodation and health insurance as well as university placement and academic, social and cultural facilities. Applications for the general round are received in a single annual period from 10 January to 20 February.

application_readiness_checklist: Decide first whether you need the general full-time scholarship (one annual window, 10 Jan – 20 Feb) or the Research Scholarship (four windows a year, including Oct–Dec).
Have your academic transcripts and diploma or enrolment certificate ready in the format TBBS accepts.
Prepare a passport or national identity document scan before registering.
If you are targeting the Merit Scholarship Programme, secure a TOEFL IBT 80/120 or IELTS 6.5/9.0 score and SAT/IB results well before the January window.
Register on the TBBS portal early in the window — the site confirms applications are free of charge, so any paid 'agent' service is not official.
Be ready to be placed at a university and department assigned by YTB rather than one you choose yourself.
common_rejection_risks: Applying for a Turkish university programme you are already enrolled in, which the official criteria list as ineligible.
Holding Turkish citizenship or having lost it — both are explicit exclusions.
Missing the single annual window: the general round closes on 20 February and there is no second general period.
Applying to the Merit Scholarship Programme without the full bundle of 90% average plus SAT/IB plus language test plus top-10 national rank.
Applying through a paid intermediary — the official application system is free of charge.
Failing the interview stage, which sits between April and June after documentary evaluation.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Travel to Türkiye beyond the one-off flight ticket the programme provides.
Living expenses in excess of the monthly stipend, and any costs during the summer period between study years.
Personal belongings, course materials and travel within Türkiye.
Family dependants' costs — the official coverage list names the scholar only.
Turkish language preparation before arrival if entering at a level that requires it.
document_audit: Confirm your transcript is complete and legible in the language TBBS requests.
Check that your diploma or enrolment certificate proves graduation or expected graduation before August of the application year.
Validate language test and SAT/IB certificates are within validity on the submission date if applying under the Merit Scholarship Programme.
Make sure the identity document used at registration matches the one in the application form.
Upload every required supporting document before submitting — the portal issues a registration code only on submit.

alerts.message: The official Application Calendar states the general application period runs 10 January – 20 February. Plan document preparation before January, because this is the only general period in the year.

The official calendar lists a Research Scholarship application period of October–December with results announced in January, so a short-term research application is the Türkiye Bursları route that is still in-window around this time of year.
The official site states applications are received online free of charge. Any fee-charging intermediary is not an official channel.
Scholarship includes university and department placement by the programme, so your preferred institution is not guaranteed even if you are awarded.

submission_workflow: Choose the correct sub-programme (general full-time, Research, Success, Arts or Merit) and note its window.
Create an account on the Türkiye Scholarships Application System (TBBS).
Complete the online application form and upload the required documents.
Submit the application to obtain the registration code; applications are free of charge.
Track evaluation (March–April), interview (April–June) and results (early August) stages.
Complete the initial procedures in August before transferring to Türkiye in September.

new_scholarship.official_source: Qatar University, Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs — Scholarships Section
new_scholarship.duration: Full-time undergraduate degree at Qatar University

new_scholarship.description: Qatar University offers an International Students Scholarship to international students who apply to its undergraduate programmes, selected on a competitive basis. Applicants must hold a high school certificate or equivalent with a minimum average of 95% and receive final acceptance from the university. The award covers full tuition and textbook fees, pays a monthly salary of 500 QAR, and includes student housing with campus transport, an annual round-trip air fare ticket and a residence permit under Qatar University sponsorship. Transfer students, visiting students, non-degree applicants and applicants seeking a second bachelor's degree are not eligible.

new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to international (non-Qatari) applicants to undergraduate programmes at Qatar University. Applicants need a high school certificate or equivalent with a minimum average of 95%, must receive final acceptance from Qatar University, must meet the admission requirements of the college applied to, and cannot hold this scholarship alongside another sponsorship or scholarship.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applicants are selected on a competitive basis and evaluated after the scholarship application deadline. The scholarship committee may consider standard test scores in English (IELTS or TOEFL) and in mathematics (SAT, ACT or the QU Math Placer), or other test scores it selects. Nominees receive an initial conditional acceptance letter, after which Qatar University applies for the student visa.
new_scholarship.english_requirement: The university requires proof of English proficiency for admission; the scholarship committee may additionally consider IELTS or TOEFL scores when ranking applicants, but no published minimum scholarship-specific score was found on the official pages read.
new_scholarship.notes: The scholarship must be used from the semester in which it is awarded; the start may be postponed by one semester with scholarship committee approval. If the recipient does not pass the first semester, the scholarship is cancelled. This record covers the International Students Scholarship only; Qatar University separately runs a Talent Scholarship and GCC States Scholarships with different eligibility rules.

programme_detail_official.description: Qatar University's International Students Scholarship is a competitive undergraduate award for international students, covering full tuition and textbook fees, a 500 QAR monthly salary, student housing with transport to and from campus, an annual round-trip air fare ticket and a residence permit sponsored by the university. Applicants must have a high school certificate or equivalent with a minimum average of 95% and must receive final acceptance from Qatar University. Applications are made through the university's online admission application during the published annual scholarship window.

application_readiness_checklist: Target the March scholarship window — the official timeline shows 1 March to 25 March, so documents must be ready before the university admission cycle opens.
Secure a high school average of at least 95%, which is the single hardest published threshold.
Apply for admission and the scholarship together in the 'Scholarship Application' section of the online admission application.
Arrange to send the original high school transcript and admission documents to the Admissions Department in Doha during the application period.
Hold IELTS or TOEFL and SAT/ACT results ready, since the scholarship committee may consider them.
Check you are not a transfer, visiting or non-degree applicant, as those categories are excluded.
common_rejection_risks: High school average below 95%.
Missing the 1–25 March window; the scholarship is applied for inside the admission application, not separately afterwards.
Transfer, visiting, non-degree or second-bachelor's applicants, who are explicitly excluded.
Holding another sponsorship or scholarship at the same time.
Failing to maintain a cumulative GPA of 3.0 out of 4.0 or completing fewer than 12 credit hours in a semester, which cancels the award.
Not passing the first semester, which terminates the scholarship.
Falling behind the graduation period set out in the study plan.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Costs not listed in the published benefit set, such as personal expenses, course materials outside the textbook allowance and local transport beyond the campus shuttle.
Visa and health-insurance costs not covered by the university sponsorship, if any are levied.
Costs of family dependants, who are not covered by the student housing offer.
Summer and winter session fees, which the continuity conditions imply fall outside the scholarship terms.
document_audit: Original high school transcript with the 95% average clearly stated.
Passport valid well beyond the intended start of study, since the university sponsors the visa.
Admission documents required by Qatar University, which the official page states are the only documents required for this scholarship.
English and mathematics test reports, in case the committee requests them.
Confirm the application appears in the 'Scholarship Application' section before the 25 March deadline.

alerts.message: The official Scholarship Timeline lists the International Students Scholarship window as 1–25 March each year, with decision announcements listed as 'TBD'. There is no second intake.
The published minimum high school average is 95%. Applicants below this should not apply through this route.
The award is cancelled for failing the first semester and requires a cumulative GPA of 3.0/4.0 and 12 credit hours per semester thereafter.
The official conditions state the applicant cannot benefit from this scholarship and another sponsorship or scholarship simultaneously.

Send the original high school transcript and required admission documents to the Admissions Department in Doha during the application period.
Await the initial conditional acceptance letter, then the university's visa application on the recipient's behalf.
Receive the final admission and scholarship decisions by email according to the published timeline.

programme_detail_official.description: The Government of Brunei Darussalam Scholarship to Foreign Students Tenable in Brunei Darussalam is a fully funded government scholarship administered by Brunei's Ministry of Foreign Affairs for foreign students taking Diploma, Undergraduate and Postgraduate Master's degrees at five Bruneian higher education institutions. The award covers tuition and enrolment fees, a monthly personal allowance of BND 500, a monthly meals allowance of BND 150, an annual book allowance of BND 600, residential college accommodation, comprehensive insurance, economy-class air travel to and from Brunei and a baggage allowance on completion of the programme. Eligibility is governed by age caps and a published English-language standard, and holders are bound by conditions including no concurrent funding, no paid employment and departure from Brunei on completion.

application_readiness_checklist: Check your age against the caps: 25 for undergraduate and diploma programmes, 35 for postgraduate master's, measured on 1 July of the course start year.
Secure the published English score — IELTS 6.0 or TOEFL 550, or Credit 6 at GCE 'O' Level or Grade 'C' in IGCSE English as a second language.
Pick an eligible programme at UBD, UNISSA, UTB, KUPU SB or Politeknik Brunei and read that institution's programme information thoroughly before applying.
Get certified true copies of all academic qualifications, testimonials and transcripts, plus certified English translations of any document not in English.
Have your birth certificate and passport certified, and secure two referees (C1 and C2) for references and recommendations.
If applying to UBD or UTB, also complete that university's own online application — the BDGS form does not replace it.
Be ready for an interview and a possible written test in English, Malay or Arabic.
common_rejection_risks: Applying more than the published deadline, which the Ministry treats as final.
Being a Brunei national or Permanent Resident, or an international student already studying or who has studied in Brunei tertiary institutions.
Exceeding the age cap on 1 July of the course start year.
Missing the separate UBD or UTB application, which is required in addition to the BDGS form.
Uncertified or untranslated supporting documents.
Holding another scholarship, grant or loan without prior written Ministry approval, which can terminate or revoke the award.
Expecting dependants' support: no marriage or child allowance is payable and no accommodation is provided for family.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Additional insurance the Ministry urges recipients to obtain for travel to Brunei and for the full duration of the scholarship, explicitly at the recipient's own expense.
Visa and travel costs beyond the economy air ticket provided in and out of Brunei.
Costs above the stated monthly personal and meals allowances, including personal expenses, course materials beyond the BND 600 book allowance and local transport.
Family accommodation and dependants' costs, which the terms explicitly exclude.
Any costs incurred before arrival or after completion of the programme, since recipients must leave Brunei immediately on completion.

Applicants submit one application in their Personal Account under one of six published categories — NUET Applicants, SAT/ACT Applicants, Olympiad winners, IB Diploma holders, A-Level/NIS Grade 12 certificate holders or NUFYP Students — and must meet that category's minimum requirement or the application is not considered. The published deadline for the 2027–2028 cycle is October 2026 with exact dates to be announced, and the last acceptable SAT and ACT sittings for financial support consideration are 5 December 2026 and 28 November 2026.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply for admission first and wait for the offer — there is no financial support application without it.
Decide on exactly one category (NUET, SAT/ACT, Olympiad, IB, A-Level/NIS Grade 12, or NUFYP) and hit its minimum; a non-matching application is simply not considered.
If using SAT or ACT for financial support, book the in-person test early enough to sit before the published last test date (ACT 28 November 2026, SAT 5 December 2026).
Take IELTS or TOEFL in person; IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT Home Edition and TOEFL PDT are not accepted, and results must not expire before 1 August 2027.
Pay the 7,000 KZT NUET fee inside the portal if choosing the NUET category, since unpaid applications are not processed.
Route the official electronic test results through the test provider and upload a scanned copy to the Personal Account.
Watch the Personal Account and the email inbox including Spam for the Admissions Office correction notification.
common_rejection_risks: Paying the admission guarantee fee, which permanently disqualifies the applicant from the financial support application.
Missing the October 2026 financial support deadline, since the exact day is not published and could fall early in the month.
Applying under a category whose minimum result is not met — the official page states such applications will not be considered.
Remote or home-edition IELTS/TOEFL results, which are explicitly not accepted.
SAT/ACT certificates that expire before 1 August 2027, or tests taken remotely.
Applying to more than one category, since only one financial support application per person is allowed.
Missing the correction notification in the Spam folder and losing the chance to fix documents.
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs: the university publishes an average monthly cost of attendance of approximately USD 400, with estimated on-campus dining around USD 300, dormitory accommodation around USD 55, transport around USD 15, laundry around USD 8, sports centre around USD 10 and additional medical insurance around USD 5.
The NUET entrance examination fee of 7,000 KZT if entering through that category.
Any gap between the aid awarded and the published tuition of USD 12,000 (Foundation Year) or USD 15,000 (undergraduate) per academic year.
Travel to and from Kazakhstan, which is not listed among the published benefits.
document_audit: Confirm the admission offer is visible in the Personal Account before starting the financial support application.
Check the selected category in the form matches the documents uploaded.
Verify the electronic IELTS/TOEFL result was sent by the test provider and that the scanned copy is also uploaded.
Verify SAT/ACT results were sent through the College Board and that the certificate has not expired before 1 August 2027.
For IB, confirm a total of 30 with 4, 4 and 5 in three Higher Level subjects.
For A-Level/NIS Grade 12, use only final certificates issued in 2025 or 2026 with not less than ABB in three subjects.
Submit well before the deadline so any correction notification can be acted on.

alerts.message: The official page publishes the financial support deadline only as 'October 2026 – To be announced later'. Treat the whole of October as the window and apply early.
Accepting the admission offer and paying the guarantee fee means the application for financial support will not be considered. Sequence matters.
SAT and ACT results are valid only if they do not expire before 1 August 2027, and the last sittings accepted for financial support consideration are 5 December 2026 (SAT) and 28 November 2026 (ACT).
IELTS Online, TOEFL iBT Home Edition and TOEFL PDT are explicitly not accepted.
The official page warns that the Admissions Office notification may land in the Spam folder and that uncorrected applications are not considered.

submission_workflow: Choose the programme (Foundation Year Program or undergraduate) and apply through admissions.nu.edu.kz.
Sit the required in-person IELTS/TOEFL and route official electronic results to Nazarbayev University.
Receive and accept the admission offer without paying the guarantee fee if financial support is intended.
Log in to the Personal Account and click 'Submit Financial Support Application' in the Admission Results section.
Select the single category under which the application will be considered.
Upload the documents confirming the result for that category.
Submit the application; no changes are possible afterwards, so verify everything before pressing submit.
Monitor email including Spam for the correction notification and meet any correction deadline.
